commits.message:
Add issue-triage agentic workflow

Creates a GitHub Agentic Workflow that automatically triages new issues:
- Labels by type (Bug, Feature, Enhancement, Documentation, Question)
- Labels by priority (High/Medium/Low)
- Identifies duplicates and comments with a link to the original
- Asks clarifying questions when description is incomplete
- Assigns issue to maintainer (stonerl)

Also adds required .gitattributes entry for lock files.

Co-authored-by: diazdesandi <17421494+diazdesandi@users.noreply.github.com>

md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+---
+description: "Triages new issues: labels by type and priority, identifies duplicates, asks clarifying questions, and assigns to the maintainer."
+on:
+  issues:
+    types: [opened]
+  roles: all
+  skip-bots: [dependabot, renovate, github-actions]
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+tools:
+  github:
+    mode: remote
+    toolsets: [default, search, labels]
+safe-outputs:
+  add-comment:
+    max: 1
+    hide-older-comments: true
+  add-labels:
+    max: 5
+  update-issue:
+    max: 1
+---
+
+# Issue Triage
+
+You are an expert issue triager for the **Thaw** macOS application repository (`stonerl/Thaw`). Thaw is a macOS app that provides enhanced HID event management for automatic cursor visibility control while typing.
+
+Your job is to triage issue #${{ github.event.issue.number }} that was just opened.
+
+**Issue title**: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
+
+Start by fetching the full issue details (body, author, existing labels) using the GitHub tools before taking any action.
+
+## Your Triage Tasks
+
+### 1. Identify the Issue Type
+
+Based on the title and body, classify the issue:
+
+- **Bug** — a defect, crash, unexpected behaviour, or regression in the app
+- **Feature** — a request for new functionality not currently in the app
+- **Enhancement** — a request to improve or extend existing functionality
+- **Documentation** — a gap, inaccuracy, or improvement needed in docs/README
+- **Question** — a usage question rather than a true bug or feature request
+
+Apply the matching label using `add-labels`. Only apply one type label. If the issue was opened via the bug report template, the "Bug" label is already set; do not duplicate it. If opened via the feature request template, "Feature" is already set.
+
+### 2. Assign a Priority Label
+
+Assess severity and impact, then apply one priority label:
+
+- **Priority: High** — crash, data loss, security issue, or severe usability regression that blocks use of the app
+- **Priority: Medium** — non-critical bug or moderate usability issue affecting a meaningful number of users
+- **Priority: Low** — minor cosmetic issue, edge-case, or low-impact enhancement request
+
+Apply the priority label using `add-labels`. If none of the priority labels exist in the repository, skip this step rather than failing.
+
+### 3. Detect Duplicates
+
+Search for existing open **and** closed issues that are similar to this one. Use the GitHub search tools to look for:
+
+- Issues with similar titles or keywords
+- Issues describing the same error, symptom, or feature
+
+If you find a duplicate:
+1. Apply the **"Duplicate"** label using `add-labels` (skip if the label does not exist)
+2. Post a comment with `add-comment` pointing to the original issue, e.g.:
+
+> 👋 Hi @{author}! This looks like it might be a duplicate of #{number}. If that issue doesn't address your situation, please let us know what's different and we'll reopen the investigation. Thanks!
+
+### 4. Ask Clarifying Questions (if needed)
+
+If the issue description is unclear or missing important information, post a single friendly comment using `add-comment`.
+
+For **bug reports**, the following information is required:
+- Clear description of the problem
+- Reliable steps to reproduce the bug
+- Expected vs. actual behaviour
+- App version (visible in the Thaw menu bar or About screen)
+- macOS version
+
+For **feature requests**, a clear description of the desired behaviour and its use case is sufficient.
+
+If clarification is needed, post a comment like:
+
+> 👋 Hi @{author}! Thanks for opening this issue. To help us investigate, could you please provide:
+>
+> - [list the missing items]
+>
+> Once we have this information we can take a closer look. Thanks!
+
+If the issue is already clear and complete, **do not** post an unnecessary comment.
+
+### 5. Assign to the Maintainer
+
+Use `update-issue` to assign the issue to the repository maintainer `stonerl`, unless the issue is a confirmed duplicate (in which case no assignment is needed).
+
+## Important Guidelines
+
+- **Be concise and friendly** in all comments. Use a helpful, welcoming tone.
+- **Do not spam**. Only post a comment if you have something useful to say (clarifying questions or duplicate notice). Never post a generic "I've triaged your issue" comment.
+- **Respect existing labels** already applied by issue templates — do not remove or duplicate them.
+- **Skip gracefully** if a label you want to apply does not exist in the repository — don't report an error.
+- **One comment at a time** — combine any clarifying questions and duplicate notice into a single comment if both apply.

commits.message:
Fix Issue Triage workflow: add graceful fallback for unavailable GitHub tools

- Fix tool name mismatch: change add-labels/add-comment/update-issue to
  add_labels/add_comment/update_issue (underscores match actual tool names)
- Make GitHub tools optional: agent can still triage using issue title/number
  when remote MCP server fails (e.g., missing Copilot token)
- Add mandatory safe-output guideline: agent must always call at least one
  safe-output tool (including missing_tool) to prevent silent failures
- Recompile lock file with gh-aw v0.68.1 (was v0.58.0) which includes
  new github_mcp_tools_with_safeoutputs_prompt.md for better tool failure handling

commits.message:
chore(github): hygiene for labels, triage, CI, and README (#803)

* chore(github): split issue vs PR type labels and add areas

Map PR Bug fix to fix so bug stays issue-report-only, add Enhancement
and product area labels, and teach triage/path labeling to use them
(including macos-27).

* fix(github): stop noop triage trackers and assign aw issues

Disable noop report-as-issue so successful no-action triage no longer
opens [aw] No-Op Runs issues, and auto-assign agentic-workflows issues
to the maintainer.

* chore(github): upgrade gh-aw to v0.82.14

Refresh the agentic-workflows agent/skill templates, pin setup actions,
migrate engine.model to top-level model, and recompile issue triage.

* docs(github): tighten contributing norms and PR shape checks

Make PR expectations explicit in the template and CONTRIBUTING, add a
non-blocking size warning with hard checks for base/title/Closes, and
refresh the README for contributors.

* fix(github): auto-close generic macOS 27 reports as #687 dupes

The search checkbox is already required; people still file Golden Gate
noise. Surface #687 in the issue chooser and templates, and teach triage
to close general 27 reports as duplicates without further maintainer work.

* feat(github): add ops area for CI and repo tooling

Catch non-product work (workflows, scripts, hygiene) under ops while
keeping CI/CD as a PR Type for what the change does.

* refactor(github): merge PR labeler and conventions into one workflow

Single pull_request_target workflow applies labels then runs shape checks
so fork PRs still get labels and we avoid duplicating PR metadata jobs.

* chore(ci): bump actions/cache to v6 and Sonar scan to v8.2.1

Also restore README HTML/media formatting while keeping the Contributing
and Frequent Issues pointers.

* chore(docs): update README to remove macOS 27 support mention and clarify PR submission guidelines

* docs(readme): unify shield style and add latest vs beta badges

Move the badge row under the pitch, use a shared slate color for static
shields, and show live latest/beta version badges so downloads are clear.

* docs(readme): add SonarCloud badge and flatten OpenSSF shield

* docs(readme): restore OpenSSF grade color and Sonar highlight badge

* docs(readme): add Works with Raycast and Droppy badges

* docs(readme): switch Works with badges to SVG at half size

* docs(readme): drop Sonar badge and regroup shield rows

* docs: clean up README formatting

Removed extra paragraph tags from the README.

* fix(github): tighten PR metadata checks and agentic workflow docs

commits.message:
docs: restyle README hero (#837)

* docs: restyle README hero

Left-aligned light/dark wordmarks as small local PNGs, centered badge
row with bold pitch underneath, Install first; demote partner chrome.

* docs(readme): point hero headers at brand-assets SVGs

* docs(readme): restore original hero pitch wording

* docs(readme): restore Trendshift, nav links, drop star history

Move beta/sponsor into badge row; keep Raycast/Droppy and contrib.rocks; add Download/Install/Roadmap/Contributing nav.

* docs: update README with installation details and links

Reformatted installation instructions and added Golden Gate status link.

* docs(readme): restructure around product positioning

Reframe the README for a product audience rather than a library one,
without losing the lean, scannable style.

- Add "Why Thaw": free, open source, no tracking, optional Screen
  Recording, notarized releases, OpenSSF practices
- Add "Integrations": Raycast, Droppy, Alfred, and thaw:// deep links,
  which were previously two unexplained badges
- Restore screenshots: one hero, the rest in a collapsed block
- Promote the highlights into a visible "Features" section and label
  the collapsed full list so it invites a click
- Correct the Screen Recording wording to "optional", matching the
  app's own limited-mode behaviour
- Move the roadmap to docs/ROADMAP.md and link it from the docs list
- Link FREQUENT_ISSUES.md, which was previously unreferenced
- Note the Accessibility requirement in Install

* docs(readme): add translation badge and update language support section

* docs: improve README description formatting

Reformatted description for better readability.

* docs(readme): tidy languages, badges, and integrations

- Rebuild the language list as a borderless grid without the 18
  per-language Crowdin progress badges. Those badges queried positional
  indices into the Crowdin stats JSON, so adding a language silently
  shifted every percentage onto the wrong row
- Restore the dual flags (de/at, gb/us, es/mx, nl/be) and use <sup>*</sup>
  for the development-branch marker, since Markdown escapes are not
  processed inside raw HTML blocks
- Add a single Crowdin badge to the top row, styled to match the others
- Move the Alfred workflow to docs/ROADMAP.md under a new Integrations
  section; the thaw:// scheme already works with Alfred today, so Alfred
  stays listed among the tools the deep links support
- Replace the zip download with the .dmg and trim the install steps

* docs: point references at the thaw-app organization

The application repository moved from stonerl/Thaw to thaw-app/Thaw.
GitHub's redirect keeps old links working, but it stops the moment
anything is created at the old path, so update the references directly.

- Rewrite repository URLs across docs, issue templates, contributing,
  security, governance, and FREQUENT_ISSUES
- Rewrite the governance prose that described the move as pending: the
  roles table, the current/target repository table, and the repository
  migration section are now written in the present tense
- Record what the transfer taught us under "Lessons from the transfer":
  GitHub Pages does not redirect across an owner transfer, and release
  asset URLs embedded in a published appcast survive only via the
  repository redirect
- Replace the resolved "app repo on a personal namespace" residual risk
  in the assurance case with the one that is now live: update delivery
  depends on a github.io path

Bundle identifiers (com.stonerl.*), the SonarCloud project key
stonerl_Thaw, funding links, and @stonerl handles are unchanged.
Info.plist and the docs describing its values are left for the rc-2
release commit so they move together.

* docs: credit translators in CREDITS.md

Translations go through Crowdin and translation PRs are not accepted, so
translators have no commits and never appear in the contributors graph or
the avatar strip in the README. Credit them explicitly instead.

- Add CREDITS.md: 65 people across 19 languages, grouped by language and
  listed alphabetically within each rather than ranked by word count
- Add scripts/generate-credits.py to rebuild the file from a Crowdin
  top-members CSV export, holding the overrides the export cannot
  express: contributors restricted to a single language, deleted
  accounts, unusable display names, and project owners whose activity
  Crowdin records outside the members report
- Link CREDITS.md from the Languages and Contributors sections and from
  the project documentation list

Members with zero translated words are omitted.
